expectations.text: Report explicitly labels symptom / proximate cause / root cause.

expectations.text: Root cause identified is the missing email normalization at write time, NOT merely 'search uses == comparison'.
expectations.evidence: Root cause: 'The raw typed email is the account identity. No normalized key exists and the store enforces no uniqueness on it.' Why 3: 'Signup stores the email exactly as the customer typed it. No code normalizes the email on write or on read.' The == is proximate only.

Skim test: the headline states what broke, the root cause, and the recommended fix in at most three sentences, with what broke in the first; the first sentence of each section carries its claim, and none is a teaser or a qualifier chain.
expectations.evidence: The headline is 3 sentences (lines 3-5). S1 says what broke ('Support search finds a customer only when the agent types the exact email casing...'), S2 gives the root cause, and S3 holds the recommended fix ('We recommend one normalized email key in app/db.py...'). That part passes. It fails only on the section-lead clause: '### Falsification of the root cause' opens 'We tried to disprove the root cause with three checks.' That is a process teaser, the same bar applied in iteration-3. Every other section lead carries its claim, e.g. Timeline 'The defect is latent since the first version of the code.' and Counterfactual '**Outcome: confirmed with survivors.**'

notes: The headline now meets the three-sentence bar (3 sentences, fix in S3). The only #13 failure is the falsification teaser lead.
Why 5 is again a detection question ('Why did nothing catch the gap before customers hit it?') rather than a causal link, the same pattern as old_skill/run-1 in iteration-3.
Counterfactual was executed in a throwaway copy, and the output block is quoted in the report. Strong evidence.
Assumptions list is the most complete of the three (7 items). Assumption 7 'Confirmed for behavior' is generous because the production schema is unseen. The report says so.
Longest of the three iteration-4 runs (2366 words), longer than every iteration-3 with_skill run.
